messages:
sophia: Quick heads-up — trying to merge Acme LoRA into 13B int4 candidate for their private deployment.

sophia: Getting KV-cache size mismatch on eval runs, and some decoding divergence vs their baseline. Anyone seen this when merging LoRAs compiled for different hf configs?

jason: Which LoRA format? peft/lorra or custom? If peft we should be careful about key ordering + dtype after quant.

maria: If it's int4 quant, we saw weird tokenization edge cases when tokenizer.pad_token != model.config.pad_token. Did you check tokenizer files?

sophia: It's peft + HuggingFace state_dict. tokenizer seems identical but their finetune used an extra BOS token at index 0.

dave: That would shift logits during generation. Quick workaround: remap tokenizer ids before eval (align bos/eos/pad), or run a tiny mapping layer.

sophia: Good call. Running quick remap now. Also: eval-pack results from our quick-eval script show PPL 9.4 vs their baseline 7.9 and hallucination rate +8% on QA set.

nora: Can you paste the eval command and config? Might be batching or max-new-tokens mismatch.

sophia: Here —
```
./tools/quick_eval.sh \
  --model checkpoints/13B-int4-lora-merged \
  --tasks acme_qapairs,acme_servicereq \
  --batch 8 --max_new_tokens 256 \
  --template acme-deploy
```

sophia: Merge command used:
```
python tools/merge_lora.py \
  --base checkpoints/13B-int4 \
  --lora acme_lora.pt \
  --out checkpoints/13B-int4-lora-merged
```

jason: Two things to check: (1) did merge_lora run in float32 & then quantize, or was it merging into already-quantized weights? (2) Are kv-cache offsets accounted for in quant kernel selection?

maria: If merged in fp32 then post-merge quant step is necessary. Merging into an already-quantized shard will misalign scales.

sophia: I merged into fp32 and then ran our quantize script. Confirming... re-running a post-merge quant now.

eval-bot: quick-eval finished: acme_qapairs: EM 72.1 -> baseline 79.6; rouge-L down 6.2; avg latency +12ms.

dave: EM drop that big suggests model drift not only token mapping. Could be LoRA training objective mismatch (classification vs generation) — check training objective and lr schedule.

nora: Also run the eval with deterministic sampling (greedy/beam) to isolate sampling noise.

sophia: Will re-run deterministic + remapped tokenizer + post-merge quant. ETA ~2h. Posting results here.

jason: Also add a tiny adapter-compat test to our onboarding checklist: verify tokenizer ids, merge path (fp32->quant), eval deterministic, kv-cache smoke (one-shot long context).

sophia: Agree. I'll open a PR with the checklist and attach the quick-eval output. Thanks all :heart:

maria: If you need me I can run a quick LoRA sanity check on smallest shard.

sophia: Appreciate it — assigning follow-ups in the thread.
